PullRequest.Title: sessions: name item actions by what they do, not the item
PullRequest.Body:
Several Agents window and Chat actions built their action IDs from the item they act on: pull request owners, repositories and numbers, artifact and reference record IDs, folder and agent file URIs, and remote host provider IDs. This changes them to IDs that say what the action does. The item stays in the action's closure. Built-in providers, environments, applications and agents keep their real ID; any other is named by its kind (`remote-agent-host`, `other`, or where an agent's file comes from), with an index or opaque number where a surface needs distinct IDs.

- Artifact, reference, pull request and issue pill actions (copy, reveal, download, remove, open changes), in the Agents window and in the Chat view's agent host pills, use one ID per action type. Their hover caches and dropdown rows only key actions within one entry.
- Pin, unpin and pinned pill actions, artifact integration pills and groups, and agent feedback pull request targets use fixed IDs, or an index where a menu lists several.
- The remote host filter names the local host and the cloud group, and `remote-agent-host` for any other host. Edit/View Agent in both mode pickers name a built-in agent, and otherwise where its file comes from (`local`, `user`, `extension`, `plugin`).
- The Sessions view filters name built-in harnesses, environments and known applications, and use `<kind>.<index>` for any other, such as a remote host's environment or a worktree. The agent sessions filters keep built-in session types and use `<kind>.<index>` for remote agent host or other types, and an index for worktrees. New Session on… names `local`, `cloud` or `remote-agent-host`.
- The workspace picker's remote host rows get an opaque per-host ID that stays stable while the picker lives, as its folder rows already did. Allowed folders reuse that folder ID. The remote rows, Dev Container mode actions and Manage entry name the local agent host, and `remote-agent-host` for any other.
- The agent host folder pickers use an index per folder or worktree choice.
- The Changes picker names changesets by their well-known ID (`branch`, `session`, `turn`, …) or `other` for a provider-defined one, via a new `getWellKnownChangesetId`.

Unchanged: IDs whose suffix is a generated UUID or a static value, and canvas IDs.

## How to test

Open each surface and check that its actions still work: copy, reveal and remove on artifact and reference pills, pin and unpin, the host filter, the Sessions view filters, New Session on… in a repository section, the workspace picker's remote hosts and Dev Container modes, the agent host folder picker, the Changes picker, and Add PR Comment in agent feedback.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` with the 25 affected suites (session artifacts, session, session chat input toolbar, artifact integration group/presentation, chat input pills, agent host session input pills, agent host folder picker and worktree folder choices, mode pickers, changes view service and actions, workspace picker, host filter, sessions list, view menu, view pane, agent feedback widget, agent sessions and viewer): 1658 passing, 2 pending.
- After the second commit: `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>` and `pnpm run valid-layers-check` passed; `./scripts/test.sh --run` with the 12 suites it touches: 1108 passing, 2 pending.
- After the review fixes: `pnpm run typecheck-client` and `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>` passed; `./scripts/test.sh --run` with the 7 suites they touch: 866 passing. The new Sessions view test fails with index-based filter IDs.
- New tests: artifact row action IDs carry no artifact data; `getWellKnownChangesetId`, the Sessions view filter IDs and the Edit/View Agent IDs keep built-in IDs and name only the kind of any other.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The insertion and absence of any eviction are directly traced; ChatViewPane owns this filter for its view lifetime. getWorktreeFilterOptions deduplicates by folder URI, and the session-change listener replaces the current options when sessions leave. The retained objects are only URI strings and numeric map entries, so the magnitude is modest and workload-dependent, not a retained session/DOM graph.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Strongly retained worktree/repository URI comparison-key strings and Map entries containing numeric action IDs.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(W_history + R_history) retained entries over the filter lifetime, after deduplication by worktree/repository URI, even if W_current remains bounded. Repeated sessions in an existing worktree do not add entries.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Persistent heap growth proportional to historical distinct worktrees rather than currently offered worktrees; old key strings cannot be reclaimed while the view remains alive.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The filter held only current worktreeOptions and disposable action registrations. Rebuilding disposed departed worktree commands; no additional map retained their URI keys indefinitely.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Worktree command IDs now require a persistent URI-key-to-number mapping. Entries survive after their worktrees disappear from the current filter options, accumulating for the lifetime of the Chat view.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 372 inserts every offered option.key into the newly added worktreeActionIds Map (line 106) via getOrSet. Before the diff, the command ID was derived directly from encodeURIComponent(option.key), with no historical ID map. updateFilterActions() clears actionDisposables, but neither it nor the session-change listener removes departed keys from the new map.
Findings.Title: Prune action IDs for worktrees that leave the filter
Findings.Impact: In a long-running Chat view that repeatedly creates and archives or deletes sessions in new worktrees, memory for every previously offered folder key remains retained even when only a small set of worktrees is still active.
Findings.Evidence: AgentSessionsFilter.registerListeners (lines 137–151) replaces worktreeOptions and rebuilds actions when the session set changes; getWorktreeOptions (line 163) excludes archived sessions. getWorktreeFilterOptions in chat/common/sessionWorktreeFolders.ts emits one option per distinct worktree URI plus its repository, not one per session. updateFilterActions (lines 234–248) disposes old commands; registerAction2 and CommandsRegistry remove registrations on disposal. The new worktreeActionIds map is only read/inserted at line 372 and has no deletion. ChatViewPane creates the filter with this._register at line 968, so closing the menu does not release it.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep IDs stable for options that remain present, but prune mappings for departed options when rebuilding. Allocate IDs with a separate monotonically increasing counter rather than Map.size so removed IDs are never reassigned to another folder while an old menu may still reference them.

Scenarios.Scenario: Long-lived Chat view: rebuild Agent Sessions provider/worktree filter commands as sessions arrive, are archived, or are deleted.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Current options and disposable commands are rebuilt synchronously before the updated filter menu is usable. Session discovery is upstream; rebuilding itself reads the in-memory model and does not request another listing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected worktree or provider exclusions through IStorageService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One preference store/remove per user filter selection; no storage write per option during rebuild.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same selection persisted the same exclusions through the same storage calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on selection, not while populating the command-ID map.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current sessions are grouped by repository and distinct worktree URI. One option is emitted per distinct worktree plus its repository. The new map accumulates those distinct keys across the entire view lifetime, not per session or per rebuild.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous event-driven rebuilding on the UI thread. No new concurrent external operations. Closing the menu does not dispose the ChatViewPane-owned filter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: IDs are reused on warm rebuilds. Cold distinct worktree keys are inserted and never evicted after their options disappear. Old command registrations are disposed, but that no longer releases the newly retained keys. Built-in providers have fixed IDs; contributed provider IDs use a separate map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: insertion, lack of eviction, URI deduplication, replacement of departed options, registration disposal, and view lifetime were all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only strings, numbers, and map entries are retained. Typical memory growth is modest; long-lived worktree-heavy windows determine its magnitude. No measured heap sizes are claimed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one low-severity introduced unbounded-retention issue at the new worktree-ID insertion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sessions View environment, application, harness, and worktree filter menus.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing structurally deduplicated menuState computes current options; autorun registers commands/context keys. Selecting a worktree waits for the existing canOpen permission check before opening one selected session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check permission and dispatch opening the chosen session through ISessionsService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one permission check and one session-opening dispatch per worktree selection; not one open per session in that folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same selected-session lookup, permission await, and opening callback ran before the action-ID change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The permission check gates opening; generation checks reject superseded selections.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist filter preferences through existing storage ownership.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A preference change on selection, not a write for each menu option.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same filter setter persisted the same selected filter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selection work; no newly introduced external operation during ID normalization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct offered filter keys after environment scoping and worktree URI grouping, rather than every session. Non-built-in filter IDs use stable opaque numbers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous reactive menu updates; asynchronous permission checking with a generation guard. Existing menu registrations are disposed on autorun replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: New filterActionIds keeps IDs stable across rebuilds. Pre-diff context keys already retained dynamic IDs: ContextKey.reset restores a defined default rather than deleting the key. The replacement shortens those IDs, so an independent materially amplified memory regression was not established here. WorktreeLastSessions remains bounded at 50 entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that only ID generation and its small mapping changed; no increased session-opening cardinality or changed permission placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured menu latency. Current option count and historical context-key retention vary with workload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression; avoid treating pre-existing context-key retention as a new issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, update, pin, and hover artifact/reference/PR/issue pills and artifact integration groups in Chat and Sessions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pill rows can render from current/fallback data without awaiting network enrichment. Hover content is built on demand; existing live models enrich it asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh shared GitHub PR, CI, review-thread, and issue presentation models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing requests are associated with unique shared model keys and endpoint/poll cycles, not every copy-action ID or rendered pill instance. Pagination may expand an endpoint fetch; the diff does not change references, refresh scheduling, or request inputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shared model references, polling ownership, and refresh calls existed before the fixed action IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous enrichment; initial fallback rendering is not gated on these requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct artifact entry IDs, grouped integration members, and unique GitHub model keys. PR CI models additionally key by head SHA. Repeated action IDs remain scoped to an individual entry's hover; pill rendering uses action/pill object identity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-model in-flight joining and shared issue polling remain unchanged; resource-details prefetch has an existing limiter of 3. No new request burst or loss of joining was found. Global transport concurrency was not independently established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CopyFeedbackActionCache still keys PR/issues by their reference keys and artifact copy actions by artifact ID plus action type. retain removes departed entries. ChatPillHoverCache retains per-entry hovers and bounds action caching within each entry. Pinned models remain keyed by entry ID, and artifact integration groups remain keyed independently of their action ID.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderer identity, per-entry hover action ownership, retained cache keys, and unchanged model acquisition/refresh paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub request durations, pagination sizes, and transport-wide concurrency are unmeasured, but none are increased by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: Fixed action IDs do not alter expensive rendering or network work, collection cardinality, or lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use pill actions: copy, reveal, download, remove, and open PR changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: External work remains inside the selected action's run closure. Downloads await filesystem resolution and transfer; removal awaits existing provider operations. Merely constructing a row does not run these actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the selected value to the clipboard or dispatch revealFileInOS.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clipboard write or reveal dispatch per invocation; no newly eager per-row calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same closure wrote/revealed the same resource once per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the invoked action crosses the boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the chosen resource and download it through FileDownload or downloadFile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial resource resolve followed by the existing transfer; folders may enumerate/read their contents and images transfer their bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical resolution and download helpers ran only when selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On-demand download latency, unchanged by action naming.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove session records through the management service or dispatch opening the chosen PR changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One removal for an ordinary artifact; grouped recorded issue IDs are removed sequentially as before. One open-changes command for the selected PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same underlying record IDs/PR ref remained in the closure and produced the same operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing sequential removal or selected-PR opening; no new fan-out from normalized IDs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One chosen artifact/reference per normal action; grouped issue removal can involve its existing set of recorded reference IDs. Folder downloads scale with contents/bytes, not the number of other pills.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ordinary actions invoke one operation. Grouped removals explicitly await each ID sequentially. Existing download helpers own transfer concurrency; it is not changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Copy feedback actions preserve their data-bearing cache keys independently of public action IDs. Existing hover caches retain only current entries. No new transfer cache or invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after action closures are unchanged, and the actual clipboard, filesystem, download, and management calls were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Transfer sizes and provider round-trip durations are workload-dependent and unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: resource identifiers were removed from action names, not from existing cache keys or action execution semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Chat and Sessions agent-mode pickers and choose Edit/View Agent.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu construction synchronously maps current modes. The new helper classifies built-in/source IDs using existing mode/product metadata; opening a file remains deferred until its toolbar action is invoked.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the selected agent resource through IEditorService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected resource per Edit/View invocation, not one file read per mode when building the picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resource-opening closure ran on selection. hasProvider was already a synchronous registry check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: File loading gates the chosen editor, not picker display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current modes with a readable URI and a registered provider. Added classification is bounded metadata/string work per eligible mode.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous menu construction; one on-demand editor-opening promise per action. Added product-service injection does not start a demonstrated heavyweight operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new filesystem cache or service query. Existing mode observables and product metadata are read; source normalization does not change agent discovery.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded metadata classification and unchanged on-demand file-opening path. No concrete heavyweight eager module initialization was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mode counts and editor loading times are unmeasured; no changed external-work multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression from the helper or import.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workspace/environment pickers, restricted folder choices, and agent-host worktree folder chips.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Picker rows render synchronously from existing data. Missing-local-workspace cleanup, host rediscovery, and cold Dev Container availability checks run asynchronously after/display alongside the picker. Selecting a local workspace waits for its existing validation; selecting a container may also await cached/in-flight availability.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check existence of recent or selected local folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per eligible recent workspace in background cleanup; one selected-folder existence check during selection validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cleanup and validation calls occupied the same paths before the new IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup is off the display critical path; selected-folder validation gates acceptance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the selected provider whether the folder supports a Dev Container.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one queued operation per cold provider-ID/URI cache key; duplicate rows/rebuilds join the stored promise. Successful false results and errors are cached; explicit retry may clear an error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider call, cache key, in-flight promise, and limiter existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous row availability; container selection can await the existing result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List agent-host sessions used to derive worktree locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listSessions call per connection/store cold or invalidated refresh, shared across its agents and returned worktree rows; zero on a valid warm cache. Concurrent refreshes join one promise; failures leave it retryable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same shared location/store discovery and cache behavior before index-based folder action IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Current locations are returned immediately; refreshed worktrees arrive later. Explicit resolveLocation may await this existing refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the local workspace folder's real path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced/cached realpath operation per workspace folder; failures permit later retry. Non-workspace folders are not retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same lazy realpath request, caching, and failure retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normal choices use current forms immediately; explicit location resolution may await forms.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Returned recent local workspaces, current remote providers, distinct allowed folder URIs, and distinct provider-plus-folder availability keys. Worktree locations are shared per window and grouped/deduplicated, not externally fetched per menu row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing local existence-check limiter is 4; Dev Container availability limiter is separately 4. Worktree location cache is shared and delayed; location-provider aggregation uses Promise.all while session-list refreshes coalesce per connection/store.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Availability cache retains booleans, errors, and in-flight promises independently of action IDs. Existing workspace IDs were already opaque for regular rows; allowed rows now reuse that same map. New remote-ID mapping retains one small entry per encountered host; ordinary host cardinality is small and no substantial resource graph is retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged expensive boundaries, cache keys, critical-path placement, and limiter values. No new I/O fan-out is attributable to the ID changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Recent-workspace/host counts and provider availability duration vary. The small new remote-ID mapping is not a demonstrated material regression for normal host counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding; do not report pre-existing regular workspace-ID retention or unchanged discovery/validation cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote-host filter selection and New Session on an environment.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menus are built from current hosts/environments. Selection still carries the real host/environment in its closure. Connect/disconnect/rediscover remain separate explicit operations; existing discovery guards prevent immediate duplicate user requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Explicitly reconnect/disconnect the selected remote or ask the existing discovery service to rediscover hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected-host reconnect/disconnect per invocation or one discovery workflow when not already discovering. Any discovery-internal host fan-out is pre-existing; the diff does not change that workflow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same real selected host IDs passed to the same service methods, with the same discovery guards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection/discovery latency is asynchronous; ordinary filter menu construction does not await it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the existing New Session action for the environment captured by the row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One environment-specific dispatch for the invoked row; no eager session creation while mapping sources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same environment was captured; only its public action-ID suffix changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only invocation starts the existing creation workflow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current host entries and environment sources, with built-in/cloud grouping preserved. Categorizing the action name does not add an operation for each host.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Menu mapping is synchronous. Rediscovery respects isDiscovering; selected-host operations remain user-driven. Internal transport concurrency is not changed by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host discovery state and selected host IDs are unchanged. Normalization keeps identifiers in the closure, without changing discovery cache ownership or retry rules.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that ID normalization does not move or multiply connection/discovery/session dispatches; invocation bodies are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote connection times and discovery-internal request counts were not measured or exhaustively modeled, but the diff changes neither.

Scenarios.Scenario: Changes picker selection and associated telemetry.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Build rows from the existing observable changeset catalog. Choosing a row updates the selected real changeset in a transaction; normalization applies only to action names and the telemetry mode field.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one version-mode telemetry event with a normalized mode string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event per selection; constant-sized mode category replaces a potentially provider-defined string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same event frequency, previously with the original changeset ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not gate catalog display or move provider data loading onto menu construction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current catalog size; helper uses a fixed seven-element set plus a turn-prefix check. No full changeset contents are serialized by the new helper.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous catalog mapping and transactional selection updates; no new asynchronous boundary in the changed code.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ChangesViewService retains existing per-session/chat selections and suppresses identical selections. Action naming does not change catalog, summary leases, or data-load cache keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setChangesetId only updates selection state and triggers its existing signal; real changeset IDs still drive it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog sizes and existing reactive loading costs are unmeasured; they are not increased by normalization.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; telemetry payload naming is bounded rather than expanded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Feedback input: choose a PR comment target and submit a review comment.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Constructing target/menu actions only maps references. Invoking a selected PR action may await target resolution, then posts the comment and refreshes review threads before clearing busy state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh selected PR details, fetch its changed-file list, and fetch selected file content at the head commit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Selected-PR resolution workflow: one shared PR refresh plus one changed-file fetch and one file-content fetch when a matching patch exists; endpoint pagination can expand the changed-file fetch. No request is added per menu row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same explicitly captured PR was resolved with the same service calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaits remain on the invoked target-resolution path, not action construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post the review comment and refresh the selected PR's review-thread model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected-PR post workflow followed by one forced review-thread refresh workflow; shared model references are disposed afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical post and refresh calls ran in the same order before index-based action IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequential awaits gate completing the selected submission; busy state prevents another submit from the same widget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read current editor text for existing range mapping against PR head content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model.getValue per invoked target resolution; unchanged with respect to PR menu count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor text was passed to target resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of existing selected-target resolution; not moved to menu rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Displayed PR references; the invoked action passes its selected PR explicitly. Target resolution filters to that PR rather than performing requests for every displayed target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous menu mapping. Selected PR resolution performs its dependent reads in sequence; submission is guarded by widget.isBusy and posts before refreshing threads. Existing service/model request joining is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Shared GitHub models still key by PR identity, not action ID. Selected target may already be resolved; no new cache miss or invalidation from the row index.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed rows alter only IDs; selected PR closures and transitive target/post workflows were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PR changed-file pagination, file sizes, and network latency vary; no measured durations or additional fan-out are asserted.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression from target action renaming.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass over the entire 33-file inventory and every diff page (all nextOffset values reached 0). Inspected surrounding cache/renderer identity, command disposal, view ownership, shared discovery, filesystem checks, limiter values, GitHub model references, selected-action boundaries, and feedback submission. Submitted one high-confidence low-severity finding for newly retained historical worktree-ID keys in AgentSessionsFilter. Omitted correctness-only ID concerns, small bounded classification costs, pre-existing retention, and unchanged I/O paths. No concrete removed performance regression with a proven introducing commit was established, so no regression-fix learning signal was submitted. Static review only; no runtime performance measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
